Our cost of revenue was $23,257,971 for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing a $8,511,230 (or 58%) increase compared to the preceding year. The increase in costs was mainly due to a significant increase in sales volume.

ga.text: General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expenses were $5,580,071 for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing a decrease of $655,860 (or 11%) as compared to $6,235,931 for the same period in 2024. The decrease was mainly contributed by a decrease in bad debt expenses.

net.heading: Net Loss Per Share
net.text: For the fiscal year 2025, net loss per share was $32.95 compared to net loss per share of $54.88 in the preceding year. There were 1,332,954 shares outstanding compared to 1,091,562 shares.

ocf.heading: Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text:
During the year ended December 31, 2025, cash flow provided by operating activities of approximately $7.8 million was mainly due to a non-cash adjustment related to depreciation and amortization of property, plant and equipment of $13.1 million, amortization of finance lease right-of-use asset of $3.1 million, accrued liabilities of $4 million, a loss on disposal of long-lived assets of $2 million, an impairment of long-lived assets of $30.1 million, and offset by a net loss of $43.9 million.

During the year ended December 31, 2024, cash flow provided by operating activities of approximately $0.68 million was mainly due to a net loss of $59.9 million, offset by a non-cash adjustment related to depreciation and amortization of property, plant and equipment of $15.82 million, impairment of long-lived assets of $6.8 million, loss on disposal of equipment of $29 million, and a decrease in account receivable of $4.26 million.

Our cost of revenue was $23,257,971 for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing a $8,511,230 (or 58%) increase compared to the preceding year. The increase in costs was mainly due to a significant increase in sales volume.

sbc.heading: Stock-based compensation
sbc.text:
We account for stock-based compensation in accordance with the fair value recognition provisions of U.S. GAAP. We use the Black- Scholes model which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions. These assumptions include estimating the length of time employees will retain their vested stock options before exercising them, the estimated volatility of our common stock price over the expected term and the number of options that will ultimately not complete their vesting requirements. The assumptions for expected volatility and expected term are the two assumptions that significantly affect the grant date fair value. Changes in expected risk-free rate of return do not significantly impact the calculation of fair value, and determining this input is not highly subjective.

We use annualized historical stock price volatility, which is deemed to be appropriate to serve as the expected volatility of our stock price and is assumed to be constant and prevailing. The expected term represents the weighted-average period that our stock options are expected to be outstanding. The expected life is based on historical option exercise pattern.

wc.heading: Accounts receivable
wc.text:
Cash collections on our accounts receivable had a major impact on our overall liquidity. The following table presents the aging analysis of our accounts receivable as of December 31, 2025 and 2024.

The overall accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2025 increased by $2,704,897, compared to those of December 31, 2024. The increase was mainly due to an increase in the amount of accounts receivable in the current period as a result of the increase in sales revenue. We have policies in place to ensure that sales are made to customers with an appropriate credit history. We perform ongoing credit evaluations on the financial condition of our customers.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
